title: Steering Vector Injection as a Jailbreak: When Interpretability Tools Become Attack Vectors

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If steering vectors used for safety monitoring can be adversarially flipped to suppress refusals, safety tooling is dual-use. This is a critical finding for the interpretability-as-safety-tool paradigm.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reproducing optimized steering vector attacks requires extracting activation directions, optimizing steering vectors, and running safety benchmarks on modified models. Needs significant GPU and model-internals expertise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Reproducing the attack and measuring refusal direction shift is defined, but comparing steered vs. unsteered models across safety benchmarks adds evaluation scope.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
